$comment: Keys that exist in en.json and DELIBERATELY have no he.json twin (MEH-2095).
The MEH-978 parity guard checks he->en; this file is what makes the en->he
direction enforceable instead of invisible. Every entry needs a reason — a
bare list would let the next en-only key in under cover of the first.
Adding a key here is a decision that it SHOULD be English-only; if it merely
lacks a translation, translate it instead.
Lives beside en-parity-guard.test.js, which is its only consumer.
search.en_notice.body: Tells an /en visitor that business listings are Hebrew-only, so an English search returns nothing. It renders only on the English UI (components/EnSearchNotice.jsx) — a Hebrew twin would be text no one can reach.
search.en_notice.cta: The 'Switch to Hebrew' action on that same English-only notice. Same reasoning: it exists to leave /en, so it never renders on /he.
